title: Platform Guardrail Catalog for Runtime Extensions
author: Aisha Kumar
body:
Purpose
-------
This document catalogs the operational guardrails we require for any runtime extension (sidecar, agent, operator, plugin) deployed in Redwood Inference platform clusters. It defines intent, enforcement mechanisms, observable signals, rollout steps, and operator runbook excerpts so runtime authors and operators can deliver extensions that meet platform SLOs, cost budgets, and safety boundaries.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all runtime-level extensions that run in platform-managed Kubernetes/GPU-hosted runtime pools (hosted/dedicated/private).
Excludes: pure client-side SDKs, ephemeral test harnesses in developer sandboxes (unless promoted to platform clusters).

Owner and Contacts
------------------
- Document owner: eng-platform (platform-services team)
- Primary contact: Aisha Kumar (eng-platform) — aisha@redwood.ai
- Reviewers: Marco Jensen (serving-runtime), Priya Shah (eng-sre), Lina Moreno (security)

Principles
----------
1. Fail closed for correctness-critical behavior; fail open for non-critical enhancements.
2. Do not increase tail-latency variance beyond the platform budget for the target tier.
3. Prefer passive observation over active mutation; any mutation requires explicit justification.
4. Enforce resource, network, and security boundaries by default.
5. Provide clear upgrade/rollback paths and developer-facing feature flags.

Guardrail Catalog (high level)
------------------------------
Each entry below includes: name, intent, threshold/guard, enforcement type, required telemetry, and rollout testing checklist.

1) CPU Budget Quota for Sidecars
- Intent: Prevent sidecar CPU from starving model-serving processes and host daemons.
- Threshold: Max 10% of host CPU on GPU nodes (rounded to nearest CPU core quota), or cgroup cpu quota equivalent.
- Enforcement: Admission controller enforces resource requests/limits; kube-eviction policy prevents overcommit.
- Telemetry: per-pod cpu_seconds_total, cpu_utilization_percentage, node_cpu_headroom, oom_kills count.
- Rollout Checklist:
  1. Local dev smoke verifying sidecar CPU <= threshold under 90th percentile load.
  2. Canary with 1% traffic for 24h against production-like traces.
  3. Automated scaling policy disabled for sidecars by default.

2) Socket and FD Limits for Agents
- Intent: Protect the serving runtime's event loop and thread pools from FD exhaustion.
- Threshold: soft limit 1024 FDs per process, hard limit 4096 for ops.
- Enforcement: PodSecurityPolicy + init container setrlimit script; kube-probes validate FD count at startup.
- Telemetry: /proc/sys/fs/file-nr sampling, process_open_fds metric, lsof sampling on critical containers.
- Rollout Checklist: unit test for descriptor leak, load test to 2x expected peak, leak detection alert created.

3) Network Egress Whitelisting and Rate Policy
- Intent: Prevent noisy extensions from saturating cluster egress or exfiltrating data.
- Threshold: Default egress bandwidth cap 10 Mbps per extension; restriction to allowed destination CIDRs.
- Enforcement: CNI policy (calico) + egress policer per namespace; egress-rate-metrics derived from tc.
- Telemetry: namespace_egress_bytes, extension_egress_bytes, rejected_egress_connections.
- Rollout Checklist: manifest contains allowed_cidrs list, staging egress verification, signed security approval for external endpoints.

4) KV / Prefix Cache Usage and TTLs
- Intent: Extensions using shared KV/prefix caches must not starve platform caching or create inconsistent reads.
- Threshold: Max 5% of total prefix-cache transient entries and per-prefix TTL <= 10m unless explicitly approved.
- Enforcement: Cache quota manager rejects writes beyond soft quota; writeback queues have precedence scheduling.
- Telemetry: cache_hit_ratio_extension, cache_write_rejects, avg_prefix_ttl_seconds.
- Rollout Checklist: synthetic workload to validate eviction behavior, canary eviction visibility.

5) Telemetry Coverage Requirement
- Intent: Every extension must emit a minimum set of telemetry for platform observability and incident triage.
- Required signals: health probe status, op latency histogram, error counters with normalized error codes, resource usage (cpu/mem/fd), unique extension id.
- Enforcement: CI validation (telemetry-lint) and admission webhook that verifies metrics endpoint responding.
- Telemetry: service:extension:health, service:extension:latency_ms_bucket, service:extension:errors_total.
- Rollout Checklist: telemetry-lint green, dashboard tile created, alert smoke test.

6) Canary Fallback & Auto-disable
- Intent: Ensure extensions that degrade SLOs can be automatically disabled with minimal impact.
- Threshold: If 5-minute rolling P99 latency for hosting service increases > 25% relative to baseline AND error_budget_burn_rate > 2x, auto-disable extension for affected slice.
- Enforcement: Operator controller monitors SLO signals and toggles a feature flag via platform-config; automatic retries blocked.
- Telemetry: host_service_p99_ms, extension_enabled{true|false}, operator_action events.
- Rollout Checklist: SLO baseline capture, synthetic regression injection, controlled auto-disable exercise.

Observability and Dashboards
---------------------------
Guidelines for dashboard tiles that must be present for every runtime extension:
- Overview tile: extension health (OK/WARN/FAIL), enabled flag, version.
- Resource tile: CPU%/memMB/FDs over time with host headroom overlay.
- Latency tile: op latency histogram and P50/P95/P99 with host baseline.
- Error tile: normalized error rates and top 5 error messages from logs.
- Egress tile (if applicable): bytes/s and destination topology map.

Recommended alert rules (examples):
- alert: Extension_Health_Failing
  expr: extension_health{status!="ok"} > 0
  for: 2m
  labels: severity=critical
  annotations: runbook link to section "Runbook: extension health failure"

- alert: Extension_Cpu_Headroom_Exceeded
  expr: (sum by(node) (node_cpu_capacity - node_cpu_allocated) < 0) and extension_cpu_utilization > 0.20
  for: 10m
  labels: severity=high

Runbooks (selected excerpts)
---------------------------
1) Runbook: extension health failure
- Symptoms: dashboard shows extension_health != ok, host P95 latency trending up.
- Owner: platform-operator oncall
- Steps:
  1) Identify extension pods: kubectl -n <ns> get pods -l extension=<id> -o wide
  2) Check health endpoint: curl -sS http://<pod>:9100/health || echo "no response"
  3) Query metrics: prometheus: up{job="extension", extension_id="<id>"}
  4) If extension reports degraded and host SLO impacted, set feature flag to false: redwoodctl feature toggle set <extension> --env production --disable --reason "auto-disable by guardrail"
  5) Capture logs: kubectl logs --since=15m -n <ns> <pod> > /tmp/extension-logs.txt and attach to incident.
  6) If disabling restores SLOs, schedule a postmortem with extension owners and follow rollout guidance.

2) Runbook: emergency rollback of extension operator
- Preconditions: operator hung during upgrade, automated disable failed.
- Steps:
  1) Scale down operator controller: kubectl -n platform-system scale deployment extension-operator --replicas=0
  2) Remove mutating admission webhook configuration temporarily: kubectl delete mutatingwebhookconfiguration extension-operator-webhook || true
  3) Revert CRDs to previous stable revision via gitops: git checkout refs/tags/stable-extension-vX && apply manifests
  4) Scale operator back up: kubectl -n platform-system scale deployment extension-operator --replicas=2
  5) Validate: all extension CRs reconcile to expected state and host SLOs recovered.

Testing and Validation Requirements
----------------------------------
Every extension must provide a test matrix and CI jobs that run at minimum:
- Unit tests demonstrating behavior under mocked failure modes.
- Integration test harness that runs in the platform staging cluster exercising: startup, graceful shutdown, FD stress test, and telemetry emission.
- Regression test that injects latency into extension code path and validates canary auto-disable (synthetic SLO monitor).
- Load test that shows CPU/memory under 1.5x expected peak.

Compatibility and API Contracts
-------------------------------
- Admission attributes: extensions must accept a well-defined pod annotation schema: extension.redwood/owner, extension.redwood/version, extension.redwood/allowed-cidrs.
- Health API: /healthz returning JSON {"status":"ok|degraded|fail","uptime_seconds":<n>,"version":"<semver>"}.
- Metrics: Prometheus exposition at :9100/metrics and labeled with extension_id and extension_version.

Roadmap and Operational Improvements
-----------------------------------
Planned 2027 initiatives related to guardrails:
- Q1: Automated guardrail simulator — synthetic agent that replays extension workloads to measure guardrail collisions with production traces.
- Q2: Guardrail-as-code library — standardized admission manifests and telemetry-lint templates.
- Q3: Operator experience: blue/green operator rollout with traffic mirroring for safe canaries.
- Q4: Cross-cluster guardrail dashboards with tenant-level impact scoring.

Retrospective Summary (lessons learned)
-------------------------------------
- Lesson: Early extensions that lacked FD limits caused cascading timeouts in the host runtime; mandatory init scripts resolved 90% of incidents.
- Lesson: Auto-disable heuristics required conservative thresholds; we migrated from instantaneous thresholds to rolling windows which reduced flapping.
- Lesson: Telemetry-lint caught 60% of integration regressions earlier, reducing canary-to-production regression incidents by 40%.

Appendix
--------
1) Example init container to set FD limits (snippet):
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: example-extension-pod
spec:
  initContainers:
  - name: fd-limiter
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh","-c","ulimit -n 1024 && echo 'limits set' "]
  containers:
  - name: extension
    image: ghcr.io/redwood/extension:latest
    ports:
    - containerPort: 9100
---

2) Telemetry-lint example rule (YAML):
- name: require-health-metric
  type: metrics_presence
  metric: service_extension_health
  labels: [extension_id, extension_version]

3) CLI examples
- Disable extension: redwoodctl feature toggle set acme-log-proxy --env production --disable --reason "slo-regression"
- Check extension health via Prometheus: promql: extension_health{extension_id="acme-log-proxy"}
